title: Activating a part that has a core charge also activates its core
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test, with a Core Charge above $0, so it has a core, and set it inactive.
  • Make sure the Search box in the top bar is the global search, which lists inventory parts.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Inactive tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  2. Click Activate parts.
  3. Click the part A row.
  4. Click Activate on the dark bar.
  5. Click Activate in the confirmation.
  6. Click the Search box in the top bar.
  7. Type Core for followed by part A's description.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The menu opens.

Step 2:

  • Bulk mode turns on and one row is listed, for part A, with no separate row for its core.

Step 3:

  • The bar reads 1 selected.

Step 4:

  • The "Activate parts?" confirmation opens.

Step 5:

  • A green message reads "1 part updated." and part A leaves the Inactive tab.

Step 6:

  • The global search opens.

Step 7:

  • The result for part A's core no longer carries the grey "Inactive" tag: the core became active together with part A.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10816 (Story 3, Activate Parts in Bulk), story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk), story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work)

  • S3-R3: “S2-R3 to S2-R10b, S2-R14 to S2-R17 and S2-N3 apply on the Inactive tab exactly as on the Active tab, with "deactivate" read as "activate". The disabled button's hover text is "Tick the parts to activate".”
  • S2-R17: “A part's core becomes inactive together with the part, in the same change.”
  • S10-R12a: “The counts include only the parts the user selected. A core that changes with its part is not counted, so changing 2 parts that both have a core reads "2 parts updated."”
  • Feature Overview, Core functionality: “A core always has the same active state and the same tracking state as the part it belongs to.”
  • S9-R18: “Global search lists inactive parts at the current location. Each carries the grey "Inactive" tag.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
